bull_bear.body:
- Linear process integration: 'Most manufacturers own processes. A smaller number own processes arranged in the order a product actually requires them' — every material moves from enquiry to finished component without leaving the enterprise, so a customer can bring a requirement rather than a drawing and hold one conversation rather than five.
- Compounding capability chain built over three decades: plating led to stamping, stamping to moulding, moulding to tooling — 'a platform assembled that way cannot be matched by acquiring any one part of it'.
- Integrated copper precision route (forging, precision machining, precision brazing and welding, silver plating): 'Very few Indian manufacturers can offer this sequence within a single enterprise' — sections are bought out, everything downstream is in-house.
- High-tech critical welding for precision ACB mechanisms — 'a capability that only a handful of global OEMs hold in-house', in applications where the consequences of failure make customers conservative about whom they qualify (high qualification-driven switching costs).
- Silver-graphite manufacturing line described as 'first in of its kind in the country', adding a distinctive capability within the LV electrical segment.
- Capacity built ahead of demand as the mechanism by which customer allocation is won: 'We do not wait to be asked. We build the capability, then earn the share.'
- Long-standing customer relationships — 'many of whom have been with us for close two to three decades' — with multi-year order visibility.
- In-house testing laboratories providing validation to customer standards, plus a dedicated product testing laboratory for Alric's first phase of manufacturing.
- Multi-location manufacturing network (Jalgaon, Nashik, Bengaluru) placing execution capacity closer to customers.
- Own market-facing premium brand (Alric) adding a second route to market on top of the contract-manufacturing platform.
- Migration to the main boards of the National Stock Exchange and BSE brought disciplines of disclosure and documentation that improved how the business is run.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration risk from dependence on a narrow OEM base — The Company explicitly frames widening the customer base as a risk-control priority: 'Deepen the OEM relationships and process capabilities on which the enterprise rests & continue to widen the customer base so that growth does not concentrate risk.' The core OEM relationships are described as 'the part everything else stands on'.
- Execution risk on converting newly created capacity into commercial output — Management states the priority is 'execution converting what we have built into customer programmes, utilisation, commercial scale and stronger returns', and commits to 'Commission and ramp up the infrastructure created during FY 2025-26, with emphasis on utilisation, productivity, quality, delivery and capital efficiency'. Returns on the FY26 investment depend on a ramp that has not yet happened.
- Commercialisation risk in new capabilities outside the established metals/plastics base — The Company flags that copper processing, critical welding, EMS and data-centre-related ODM initiatives must still 'move from capability creation towards commercial execution and scale' — they are disclosed as capabilities created, not yet as commercial businesses.
- Brand-entry risk in scaling the Alric own-brand business against established incumbents — Disclosed as 'Establish the brand in a market of established incumbents - expanding the product portfolio, building channel depth and product availability, and progressively utilising the manufacturing and testing platform created for it. A brand is earned slowly, and we have planned for that.' This is a departure from the contract-manufacturing model and carries channel-build and utilisation risk.
- Organisational scaling risk — leadership depth, systems and governance must keep pace with growing complexity — The Company commits to 'Continue building leadership depth, systems, governance, technological readiness and execution discipline as the enterprise grows in scale and complexity', acknowledging that institutional capacity is a constraint on the growth path.
- Working capital, capital-allocation and return-on-capital discipline under a growth and capex cycle — Stated as an explicit watch-item: 'Growth will remain anchored in operating profitability, working-capital discipline, cash generation, return on capital and disciplined allocation of investment.' The Board separately declined to recommend any dividend for FY2025-26, retaining cash for the business.
- Enterprise risk management dependent on a recently constituted committee and framework — The Risk Management Committee was constituted only on 12/11/2024 under Regulation 21 of the SEBI Listing Regulations and held just two meetings in FY2025-26 (26/09/2025 and 15/03/2026). The Company states it has 'established a robust mechanism to keep Board Members informed about risk assessment and mitigation procedures' and formulated a Policy on Risk Management, but the AR text does not enumerate the specific risks identified under that framework.
- Balance-sheet leverage requiring post-year-end equity fund-raising — Disclosed under Material Changes and Commitments: a preferential issue of equity shares and convertible warrants aggregating approximately Rs.325 Crores after the financial year end, which the Company states 'is expected to strengthen the Company's capital structure and financial position through reduction of its debt obligations' — indicating debt obligations material enough to require an equity raise to reduce.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company is engaged in the manufacture of electrical and allied engineering components, assemblies and products, with output spanning components, sub-assemblies and complete products manufactured to the specifications of a number of original equipment manufacturers across several applications. Revenue arises predominantly from business-to-business relationships with OEMs, and the business is described by application area and capability deployed rather than by conventional segment. During FY2025-26 the Company added a second, market-facing route through Alric Electric Private Limited, a premium own-brand electrical products business acquired and formally launched in March 2026, for which Spectrum is the manufacturing and engineering platform.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Low-voltage switchgear:** Precision components, Enclosures, Current-carrying parts and assemblies, Switchgear Products
- **High-voltage and power distribution:** Specialized components, Copper-based current-carrying parts
- **Distribution boards and control panels:** Metal Distribution Boards, Metal, Plastic Distribution Boards, Modular Electric Board Panels, Control Panels, Complete products and assemblies
- **Electric mobility infrastructure:** EV Charger (charging equipment developed in-house)
- **Renewable energy and industrial automation:** Control panels and associated assemblies
- **Medical electromechanical:** Sub-assemblies developed under collaboration
- **Tools, Molds & Dies:** Tools, Molds, Dies
- **Own-brand electrical products (Alric Electric Private Limited):** Alric, Protection devices including MCBs and RCCBs, Distribution boards, Wiring devices, Wiring accessories, Electrical Safety Devices

outlook.body:
- Build capability ahead of customer demand rather than floor space alone — developing specialised capabilities across copper forging, machining, precision brazing, welding and silver plating to create an integrated route to high-performance, customer-ready components.
- Deepen the integrated OEM/B2B manufacturing core, which management states remains the backbone of the growth strategy, by strengthening integrated and specialised capabilities within a common quality system.
- Extend the value-capture model from contract manufacturing and integrated engineering solutions, through ODM, to proprietary products, brands and channels — with the acquisition of Alric Electric Private Limited creating a market-facing premium electrical brand and a strategic entry into the LV electrical segment.
- Build new platforms in EMS (Electronic Manufacturing Services), data-centre solutions and product development, and participate more meaningfully in the value created through ODM and Alric.
- Invest in technology, design, engineering, product development, testing and research infrastructure to conceive, validate and industrialise products with greater speed and technical depth.
- Expand the multi-location manufacturing network — integrated infrastructure at Jalgaon towards approximately 3 lakh sq. ft. under one roof, with new infrastructure commissioned at Nashik and Bengaluru.
- Integrate renewable energy into operations and shift environmental disclosure from certification-led assurance towards performance-based, outcome-based reporting.
- Continue to invest in leadership depth, technical talent and project-execution capability, building capability before it is needed rather than after.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body:
FY2025-26 was described by management as a year of deliberate investment at a scale larger than any previous phase in Spectrum's journey, building for process integration, technological depth and higher-value applications rather than floor space alone. The Jalgaon mother location was expanded towards approximately 3 lakh sq. ft. of integrated smart manufacturing infrastructure under one roof, and new infrastructure was commissioned at Nashik and Bengaluru, strengthening the multi-location manufacturing network and expanding execution capacity closer to customers. Shop-floor investments included inline automatic inspection on critical parts replacing manual checking entirely, robotic handling on multi-cavity moulding, quick tool/mould changeover with Poka-yoke mistake proofing, and validation to customer standards in Spectrum's own testing laboratories.

Four initiatives sit beyond the established process map, with FY2025-26 laying the foundations and FY2026-27 stated to be about commissioning, commercialisation and ramp-up. (1) Electronic Manufacturing Services — status 'Project Conceived' — envisages an investment of approximately Rs 20 crore and around 40,000 sq. ft. of dedicated infrastructure to support advanced electronics manufacturing across components, sub-assemblies and higher-value electronic products; the CMD's letter states the project is moving from conception to an advanced stage of execution in FY2026-27, with commercialisation and ramp-up expected to progress through the year ahead. (2) Copper, an integrated precision route — status 'commissioning' — combining copper forging, precision machining, precision brazing and welding and silver plating into an integrated route to a customer-ready precision component, with sections bought out and everything downstream in-house. (3) High-tech critical welding for precision ACB (air circuit breaker) mechanisms — status 'Commissioned'. (4) Data-centre products and solutions through the ODM route — status 'activity commencing in FY2026-27' — with approximately 1 lakh sq. ft. being allocated to the opportunity, developed through deeper collaboration with global OEM partners.

A silver-graphite manufacturing line, described as the first of its kind in the country, adds a distinctive capability within the LV electrical segment. On the inorganic side, Spectrum acquired Alric Electric Pvt. Ltd., which became a wholly owned subsidiary with effect from 06/03/2026 and was formally launched in March 2026, bringing a market-facing premium electrical products brand into the enterprise as a second route to market alongside the B2B/OEM core.

On energy infrastructure, a 1.34 MW renewable solar installation at Jalgaon is operational and a further 3.0 MW is planned during FY2026-27, taking total solar capacity to 4.34 MW. Funding context: QIP proceeds of Rs 3,654.59 lakhs (allocated Rs 1,375.00 lakhs to Capital Expenditure) were fully utilised as at 31 March 2026 with nil pending utilisation, and subsequent to year end the Company raised approximately Rs 325 Crores through a preferential issue of equity shares and convertible warrants, expected to strengthen the capital structure through reduction of debt obligations. Management explicitly flags execution risk associated with a capital programme of this scale.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management positions Spectrum as one of the few integrated partners capable of serving demanding requirements in the OEM supply-chain ecosystem, with linear process integration (plating, stamping, moulding, tooling) that lets a customer bring a requirement rather than a drawing and hold one conversation rather than five.
- Capability additions — copper forging/machining/precision brazing/welding/silver plating, and specialised precision welding for critical air circuit breaker mechanisms — are stated to enable Spectrum to address more complex and technology-intensive customer requirements.
- The silver-graphite manufacturing line is described as first of its kind in the country, adding a distinctive capability within the LV electrical segment.
- Alric is expected over time to add a complementary market-facing revenue stream to the business model, diversifying away from pure B2B contract manufacturing.
- Management states India's electronics manufacturing requirement is growing faster than domestic capacity can absorb it, and the disciplines EMS demands — precision, traceability, process control, testing — are disciplines the existing platform already runs.
- High-tech critical welding for precision ACB mechanisms is described as a capability only a handful of global OEMs hold in-house, which is why those who do not come to Spectrum.
- Customer concentration is acknowledged: a substantial share of revenue is derived from a limited number of multinational customers, managed through long-standing relationships, multi-year order visibility and new-account development.
- FY2025-26 laid the foundations; FY2026-27 is stated to be about commissioning, commercialisation and ramp-up of the new platforms.
- Customer concentration is "managed through long-standing customer relationships, multi-year order visibility, new-account development and the continued broadening of our capability base." — a qualitative reference to multi-year order visibility; no order-book quantum is disclosed.

sk.overview: The DRHP frames Dies and Moulds as a segment of India's Tooling Market and as the backbone for precision manufacturing of plastic moulding products across automotive, pipe fittings, industrial components and electronics. Per the Ken Research Report the India Dies and Moulds Market was valued at INR 45,400 crore in FY'25 and is projected to grow at an 11.5% CAGR to FY'30F, with Automotive Moulds the largest application at INR 25.2 thousand crore in FY'25 and B2B/OEM the dominant distribution channel. Demand is presented as being pulled by India's industrial and infrastructure cycle - Union …
